record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: Given an instance I of the Stable Marriage problem with ties, determine whether there exists an efficient output-sensitive algorithm for listing all stable matchings in time O(p(n) + |S_I| q(n)), where p and q are polynomial functions and S_I is the set of stable matchings of I.

evidence.quote: it is an open problem as to whether there is an efficient algorithm for listing all stable matchings, given an instance I of smt of size n. By efficient, we mean that the algorithm should have complexity O(p(n) + |S_I|q(n)), where p and q are polynomial functions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An instance I of the Stable Marriage problem with ties (SMT) consists of a set of n men and n women, together with, for each person, a preference list ranking some subset of the members of the opposite sex, where ties are allowed (i.e., a person may rank several alternatives as equally preferred). A matching M is a set of disjoint man–woman pairs. A pair (m,w) not in M is a (weakly) blocking pair for M if m and w each strictly prefer each other to their current partner under M (with unmatched persons treated as worst). A matching M is weakly stable if it admits no blocking pair. Let S_I denote the set of all weakly stable matchings of I, and let n denote the size of I.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given any instance I of SMT, outputs every matching in S_I (each exactly once) within total running time
  O(p(n) + |S_I| · q(n)),
where p and q are fixed polynomials? Equivalently, is there an output-sensitive polynomial-delay algorithm for enumerating all weakly stable matchings of an SMT instance?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any algorithm that enumerates all weakly stable matchings of a stable marriage instance with ties in output-sensitive polynomial time O(p(n)+|S_I|q(n)). While polynomial-delay enumeration is known for the classical stable marriage problem (without ties) via Gusfield's method on the rotation poset, no analogous output-sensitive result for SMT appears in the literature, and the question is repeatedly cited as open in surveys on matching under preferences.

status_evidence.title: Stable marriage with indifference - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses notions of stability (weak, super, strong) under ties but mentions no output-sensitive enumeration algorithm for weakly stable matchings.
status_evidence.claim: No output-sensitive enumeration algorithm for weakly stable matchings in SMT is documented.

status_evidence.title: A Study of Stable Marriage Problems With Ties (Scott)
status_evidence.snippet: Thesis on SMT structure and algorithms; enumeration of weakly stable matchings in output-sensitive time is not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference on SMT does not provide an output-sensitive enumeration algorithm.
